author: Zane Douglas
title: Crimson fall in semifinals in overtime thriller - NewsBreak
text:
By Zane Douglas ,
9 hours ago
Maple Grove played Andover in the semifinals of the Section 5AA boys hockey tournament and lost in overtime after a chippy game.
The Crimson's season ended on Feb. 21 following an overtime loss to the Huskies in a game with a lot of stoppages, penalties and shoving.
Despite being the top seed in the tournament, the Crimson were on their heels the entire first period. The Huskies outshot the Crimson 12-1 in the first period, controlling the puck and the offensive zone for much of the time.
Crimson goalie Ryder Skanson kept the team afloat with some excellent saves in the first period, allowing for a bounce back second frame. The Crimson pretty much entirely flipped the game around playing aggressive on offense and outshooting the Huskies 9-4. They also added a goal to take the lead and shut the Huskies out for another period.
Senior forward Lane Glende scored first in the game off of an assist from Wyatt Kuznik. Glende scored in the first minute of the second period. Skanson held the Huskies scoreless again and put the Crimson in a good spot to win heading into the final 18 minutes.
The third period was filled with intense hits, offense and some pen game-changing calls from officials. Andover scored in the first five minutes to tie the game. Brody Peterson tied the game to the tune of a roar from the loud Andover crowd.
Less than a minute later, Camden Langfield of the Huskies ran into Skanson in the crease and was panelized with interference. Just 14 seconds later, Maple Grove's Cole Anderson rifled one past goalie Wyatt Riemer. Kuznik and Grady Karnz assisted on the tiebreaking score.
The Huskies started to play more aggressive, racking up shots until finally Jack Rykkeli snuck one past Skanson's left side on a wrist shot. Peterson and Dillon Larsen assisted and before the Crimson had a chance to breathe, the Huskies scored again. Only this time they didn't.
Referees blew the play dead after the Husky skater rammed into the goalie forcing the puck in. It was a close call, but the controversial call drew the ire of the Andover faithful.
The rest of the third period was scoreless, and the five seeded Huskies would take the Crimson to overtime. The Huskies controlled overtime from the start. After a few shots, senior defenseman Chase Nadeau scored the game-winning goal with 3:35 left in the period. Peterson and Larsen assisted on the goal.
The upset ended the Crimson's season at 16-9-2.
